correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed from the coordinate model. The facet plane gives \(r^2=abc/(ab+bc+ca)\), the vertex norm gives \(R^2=a+b+c\), and the edge formula gives \(q=((a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2)/(2(a+b+c)^2)\). After normalization, fixed \(q\) is a circle with the stated cosine parameterization; direct multiplication yields the exact \(\cos(3\theta)\) law. Positivity of the normalized coordinates gives the sharp \(q=1/4\) phase transition. The bundled verifier independently checks the geometric formulas, parameterization, endpoint branches, and pointwise bounds. Numerical checks are supporting evidence only; the proof establishes all quantifiers.

value.rationale: The radius ratio \(r/R\) is a natural scale-free measure of tetrahedral regularity, while \(q\) is a symmetric scale-free measure of how unequal the three opposite-edge-pair lengths are. The result gives the entire feasible radius-quality range at each \(q\), not just an isolated inequality, identifies both equality families, and locates the exact \(q=1/4\) transition at which degeneration becomes compatible with the prescribed anisotropy. This is a structural classification of a classical geometric family rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
